executiveSummary: GM1734's official 2025 identity, generalized boundary, contained reference point, 48,945 residents, 90 neighbourhoods, twelve BAG woonplaatsen, 25 BRT settlement labels and Gelderland-Midden safety-region assignment are coherent. Neighbourhood rows sum to 48,930, fifteen below the municipality total (-0.031%), which is compatible with small-area rounding. All ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services satisfy the deterministic arithmetic contract, but the local interpretation is not release-ready. The river preset reports a 2.391544 legacy depth-like amplitude, 20,199 affected resident-equivalents at T+24 and 21,567 through T+72 without a selected Rhine/Waal/Linge/dike-ring-43 scenario, breach, arrival time, defence state or licensed inundation field; this diagnostic must never be labelled metres. Nine materially different active presets reuse nearly the same neighbourhood ordering. Pluvial and drought behavior omit the Linge, groundwater, streefpeil/GGOR, soil, drainage and live control states. Static water, grid, antenna, school, road, rail, ferry and care records do not establish incident-time operation, capacity or restoration. Betuweroute hazardous-goods context, transient event/recreation exposure, external acute care and cross-river/cross-region access are not causally represented. Observations, forecasts, plans, historic events, registers, scenarios and synthetic indices retain their own validity and scope; missing T+48/T+72 water forecasts and absent live operator state are Unknown/NoData, never zero, safe, open, available or restored.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM1734 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, woonplaats and settlement input
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; BAG/PDOK snapshot retrieved 2026-08-31; BRT source date 2025-07-01
supports: CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK input identifies GM1734 as Overbetuwe in Gelderland and reports 48,945 residents, density 449/km2, 21.7% aged 65 or older and 5,876 one-person households. The generated reference point [5.775960919270877, 51.91890585111392] is inside the generalized boundary.

Ninety neighbourhood rows in nineteen districts sum to 48,930 residents, fifteen below the municipality total (-0.031%); households sum to 20,590 and rounded age-65-plus rows to 10,610. Reconciliation must not rewrite rounded observations.

All twelve BAG woonplaatsen—Andelst, Driel, Elst, Hemmen, Herveld, Heteren, Homoet, Oosterhout, Randwijk, Slijk-Ewijk, Valburg and Zetten—are contained. Twenty-five BRT labels independently distinguish thirteen woonkernen, two deelkernen, one gehucht and nine buurtschappen. BAG is Public Domain Mark 1.0.

District heating and public charging cover 0/90 rows, cars per household 61/90, average home value and related housing fields 78/90, address density 89/90, and GP/supermarket proximity 82/90. Missing, suppressed, not-applicable and published zero remain distinct.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Streefpeilenplan Over-Betuwe
evidenceSources.edition: plan fixed 2025-05-27; current project page accessed 2026-09-03; reuse licence not stated
supports: The 17,311-hectare planning area lies between Nederrijn, Waal, Pannerdensch Kanaal and a western canal connecting the Linge to the Nederrijn, spans parts of Overbetuwe and four neighbouring municipalities, and identifies the Linge as the central important watercourse.

The water board uses target levels rather than a binding peilbesluit because height and soil make water supply and retention difficult. Dry periods can produce levels below target; targets are best efforts, and even a peilbesluit can temporarily fail in extreme weather or emergencies.

The GGOR method considers groundwater and surface water against land use. The adopted plan and peilenkaart are governance/design evidence, not an observation, forecast, current pump/weir position, incident capacity or proof of safety.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Dijkversterking Sprok–Sterreschans–Heteren and Elden–Heteren segment
evidenceSources.edition: current project pages accessed 2026-09-03; exploration 2024-2027; reuse licence not stated
supports: The Sprok–Sterreschans–Heteren project follows the Waal, Pannerdensch Kanaal and Nederrijn. The Elden–Heteren segment is about 8.5 km and project material identifies stability and piping reinforcement needs over parts of the alignment.

The water board says the dike is currently safe while its latest assessment finds parts do not meet the future statutory standard; exploration continues through 2027 and planning/construction follow later.
This is long-horizon assessment and project-stage context. It is not a current failure, breach, overtopping observation, defence reliability percentage, arrival-time forecast or inundation footprint.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Regional risk profile and crisis-planning context
evidenceSources.edition: definitive regional risk profile published 2025; current page accessed 2026-09-03; reuse licence not stated
supports: VGGM identifies flooding and epidemic/pandemic as the largest regional risks, followed by nature fire, cyber disruption, utility disruption and animal disease.

The definitive profile records transport of toxic liquids and gases by road, rail and water and treats the Betuweroute as a hazardous-goods corridor with preparative access and incident-response arrangements.

Earlier official dike-ring-43 planning identifies Arnhem, Lingewaard and Overbetuwe on the eastern part of the Betuwe/Tieler/Culemborgerwaarden ring and requires interregional coordination with Gelderland-Zuid. The older plan must be revalidated before operational use.
A regional risk category or adopted plan is an official scenario/governance class, not an incident observation, municipal probability, live resource roster or T+72 forecast.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Climate adaptation, ferry links and dated transport/event lifecycle evidence
evidenceSources.edition: current municipal pages accessed 2026-09-03; dated Vierdaagse page 2026-07-21 and Betuweroute liveblog 2026-04-10; reuse licence not stated
supports: The municipality lists year-round Lexkesveer between Randwijk and Wageningen, a year-round Driel foot/bicycle ferry to Doorwerth/Oosterbeek, and seasonal foot/bicycle ferries from Slijk-Ewijk to Beuningen and Heteren to Renkum. Route existence does not prove schedule, water-level operability, vessel availability or emergency capacity.
Municipal climate-adaptation information treats water nuisance, drought and heat as distinct pathways. It is planning/preparedness context rather than selected forcing or measured performance.

The 2026 Vierdaagse page documents temporary Tielsestraat closure, routes toward A325/A50/A15, calamity routes for Oosterhout, Valburg and Elst, and P+R Elst. This past event demonstrates transient population and time-varying routing but must not persist as a current closure.

A 2026-04-10 municipal liveblog records a Valburg protest that stopped Betuweroute freight from about 12:15 until the action ended around 20:00, after which ProRail worked to resume traffic. It is closed historical lifecycle evidence, not a current disruption.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — NWB-Light, rail and scheduled-transit context consumed by the simulator
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 2026-08-01; ProRail/OVapi snapshots retrieved 2026-08-31/2026-09-03; NWB and ProRail public geometry CC0 1.0
supports: Eight logical border links encode A15 links toward Neder-Betuwe, Lingewaard and Nijmegen, A50 links toward Beuningen and Renkum, A325 links toward Arnhem and Lingewaard, and N837 toward Arnhem. Same-corridor A15, A50 and A325 sections are series relationships, not additive capacity.

Nominal values 260 for trunk links and 150 for the regional link are synthetic scenario units, not measured emergency throughput. Route eligibility is limited to Mobility/Supply and does not describe utility or ambulance topology.

Elst and Zetten-Andelst stations and 95 GTFS stop areas establish static/scheduled context only. They do not prove incident-time train/bus operation, freight state, rolling stock, replacement transport, evacuation capacity or accessible boarding.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Dutch water boards; Netbeheer Nederland; Rijksinspectie Digitale Infrastructuur; DUO
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Public water-control, electricity-capacity, antenna and education register context
evidenceSources.edition: deployment snapshots retrieved 2026-09-02/03; HWH CC BY-SA 4.0; NBNL/RDI/DUO source-specific public terms; exact municipal coverage and cadence vary
supports: Two hundred six HWH points are assigned inside GM1734: twelve sewer pumps, thirteen surface-water pumps, RWZI Zetten and 180 weirs. Capacity is present for nine sewer and seven surface-water pumps; most weir capacities and RWZI capacity are null.

RG Zetten and RG Andelst include legacy 'buiten bedrijf' records with numeric capacities alongside realised records. Without stable asset identity, manager confirmation and valid time, these are ambiguous register lifecycles, not proof that current pumping is failed or available.

One Liander NBNL sample at postcode 6675BB reports station-planning values, queues, TenneT class 3/3 and projects with earliest year 2030. It is capacity-planning context, not GM1734 feeder coverage, live load, outage, damage, switching or restoration.

The context contains 110 RDI antenna sites and 35 DUO education locations. Installations/registrations do not establish coverage, traffic, backhaul, battery endurance, occupancy, shelter designation, accessibility or incident-time operation.

evidenceSources.title: E08 — Driel water observations and short-range forecasts
evidenceSources.edition: observations valid 2026-09-02T17:30:00Z; forecasts through T+24 retrieved in the deployed 2026-09-03 snapshot; public-data reuse context is CC0 unless stated by the dataset
supports: Two timestamped observations report Driel beneden at 614 cm NAP classified normal and Driel boven at 646 cm NAP classified lowered. They are point observations with their own valid time, not municipality-wide water state.

Forecasts exist only through T+24: Driel boven discharge 17 m3/s at T+1/6/12/24, Driel beneden level 612 cm NAP, and Driel boven level 643/643/643/641 cm NAP. The source classification remains normal/lowered as applicable.
T+48 and T+72 are NoData and must not be extrapolated. Observation/forecast values are not breach, flood extent, depth, drainage capacity or proof of safe/dry neighbourhoods.

evidenceSources.title: E09 — External acute-care roles nearest the municipality reference point
evidenceSources.edition: questionnaire version 1.1 published 2026-07-03 and retrieved 2026-09-02; CC0 1.0
supports: No acute-care point is assigned inside GM1734. Straight-line reference-point distances are approximately 11.916 km to Canisius-Wilhelmina Ziekenhuis, 12.103 km to Radboudumc, 12.893 km to Rijnstate, 14.572 km to Gelderse Vallei and 24.941 km to Ziekenhuis Rivierenland.

RIVM facility roles are static questionnaire context. Straight-line distance and a registered 24/7 emergency-department role do not establish ambulance time, bridge/road state, acceptance, staff, beds, generator endurance, diversion or T+72 capacity.
Absence of a point inside the generalized boundary means no assigned record in this dataset, not no local care, no vulnerable population or zero care demand.

evidenceSources.publisher: Veiligheids- en Gezondheidsregio Gelderland-Midden / Park Lingezegen
evidenceSources.title: E10 — Nature-fire preparedness and recreation/access context
evidenceSources.edition: current public preparedness and area-management pages accessed 2026-09-03; reuse licences not stated
supports: VGGM explains that nature-fire phase is a preparedness risk indicator and that dry, windy conditions can produce rapid, unpredictable spread; access routes, area management, signage and evacuation planning matter.

Park Lingezegen identifies Waterrijk-West as a water/reed nature and recreation area with a three-kilometre accessible route for wheelchairs and mobility scooters. Municipal recreation pages also identify Landgoed Loenen and old river-course landscapes.
Preparedness phase and land-cover/access context are not ignition, perimeter, flame intensity, plume, visitor occupancy, route state, extinguishing-water inventory, suppression resource or all-clear.

identity.summary: GM1734, Overbetuwe, Gelderland and safety region Gelderland-Midden agree across the consumed official 2025 sources.
notes: Feature id, bundle code and bundle name match; the safety-region assignment is unique.
Identity verification does not establish hazard, lifeline or operational calibration.

geography.summary: The official generalized boundary, generated reference point and contained place geometry are internally coherent.
notes: The audit context reports [5.775960919270877, 51.91890585111392] inside the boundary; all twelve BAG place centres are contained.
Administrative containment does not encode Rhine/Waal/Linge hydraulics, dike-ring-43 compartments, terrain, groundwater, drainage, Betuweroute barriers or incident footprints.

demography.summary: Municipality and neighbourhood population totals reconcile within CBS small-area rounding.
notes: Municipality population is 48,945; ninety neighbourhoods sum to 48,930, a fifteen-person difference (-0.031%).
Age 65+ is 21.7% and 5,876 one-person households matter for contact, assistance and evacuation demand, not automatic restoration priority.
Resident totals omit event-time rail/ferry users, Vierdaagse participants, recreational visitors, workers and institutional populations. Missing incident-time presence remains Unknown.

regionalDetail.summary: All ninety neighbourhoods are represented, but multiple socio-economic fields and dynamic exposure are incomplete.
notes: Lingebuurt is the largest row at 2,325, followed by Kern Herveld 2,115 and Kern Oosterhout 2,045; distinct villages, rural rows, rail/industrial areas and nature/recreation areas remain visible.
District heat/public charging cover 0/90, cars per household 61/90, housing/value fields 78/90 and GP/supermarket proximity 82/90. Missing coverage is not zero infrastructure or zero need.
School and antenna points, parks and dated events are context only; no live occupancy, accessibility or responder-resource data is present.

settlements.summary: Twelve BAG woonplaatsen and 25 BRT settlement labels provide coherent but differently scoped place context.
notes: BAG administrative woonplaatsen and BRT settlement morphology are retained independently.
Settlement labels and metadata are descriptive and are not forced to reconcile with CBS residents.

transport.summary: Major road, station, stop and ferry identities are useful, but the graph cannot establish incident-time access, capacity or cross-river continuity.
notes: Eight logical border links omit internal village/rural roads, bridges, tunnels, grade-separated crossings and ferries. Same-corridor A15/A50/A325 segments and nominal capacities cannot be summed as independent emergency routes.
Elst and Zetten-Andelst stations and 95 scheduled stops are not live service. Betuweroute freight/hazardous-goods traffic is not represented by passenger station points.
External hospital routes, water-level ferry constraints, vehicle/crew availability, closures and destination acceptance are absent and remain Unknown.

emergencyContext.summary: Authoritative flood, water, fire, hazardous-goods and preparedness context exists, but live command, resources and first-72-hour decisions are absent.
notes: VGGM prioritizes flood, nature fire, cyber and utility disruption; dike-ring-43 and Betuweroute conditions require cross-region/operator coordination.

The simulator has no selected breach/control case, live asset state, ignition/perimeter, visitor count, rail/road/ferry status, hospital acceptance, support-point inventory or operator restoration ledger.
Plans, future reinforcement, historical disruption, dated observations, T+24 forecast and partial registers keep their own validity; none automatically becomes a T+72 operational fact.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten presets execute at all checkpoints, but river, pluvial, wildfire, cyber, heat and compound outputs contain release-blocking local claims.
notes: The focused gate exercised severe-storm, pluvial-flood, river-flood, coastal-flood, heatwave, winter-storm, cyberattack, earthquake, wildfire and compound at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.

River-flood at T+24 gives severity 0.747882, legacy depth-like amplitude 2.391544, pressure 0.432910, 20,199 affected and 411,613.511 deprived person-hours; at T+72 it still gives 21,567 affected and 1,567,825.875 person-hours. This field is explicitly not hydraulic metres.

Pluvial T+24 gives severity 0.264831, amplitude 0.366688, 3,831 affected, Drainage 0.573926 and 158,573.604 person-hours; at T+72 affected is zero despite 321,783.114 cumulative person-hours, without local water-system milestones.

Wildfire T+24 gives zero local flame but smoke 0.472002, severity 0.175114 and 1,825 affected without an ignition or plume. Cyber T+24 gives severity 0.473783 and 12,165 affected without a named target or topology.

Compound T+72 retains amplitude 0.378685, pressure 0.479940, 23,442 affected and 1,599,507.423 person-hours. Coastal direct flooding and remote earthquake ground motion are zero, but only for those named direct screens.

numericalInvariants.summary: The deterministic contract passes boundedness, population/service reconciliation, causal-ledger closure and monotonic cumulative burden.
notes: Initial command MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM1734 pnpm audit:model passed one file and two tests.
Controlled probes produced finite/bounded service values, integral bounded affected population and monotonic deprived person-hours at all six checkpoints.
Passing arithmetic proves implementation consistency, not physical calibration, evidence validity, forecast skill or operational readiness.

spatialPlausibility.summary: A common seeded surface overrides distinct river, pluvial, wind, heat, winter, cyber and fire mechanisms.
notes: At T+24, materially different active presets reuse the same or nearly the same leading neighbourhoods: Lingebuurt, Kern Herveld or Kern Oosterhout, Groenoord and de Wuurde. The full order is shared across most hazards.

River/pluvial allocation does not follow selected dike-ring compartments, river/stream flow paths, elevation, soils, drainage or defence state; wildfire does not follow an ignition, eligible fuels, barriers or valid wind; cyber does not follow a named asset/network.
The model labels river/coastal spatial evidence derived-screening and the others synthetic. Neither class supports parcel/neighbourhood hotspot precision.

serviceDependencies.summary: Exact eight-service trajectories exceed available water, grid, telecom, transport, supply and care topology/state evidence.
notes: Two hundred six HWH points identify static water assets but not catchments, dependable units, control positions, inflow/quality, power dependency, redundancy or repair state.
One NBNL sample, 110 antenna sites and 35 education records cannot support municipality-wide power, gas, telecom, facilities or shelter trajectories.
Mobility/Supply depend on eight logical road proxies; rail, ferries, internal routes, water crossings, hazardous-goods restrictions and external-care acceptance do not drive availability.
No local acute-care point exists in the consumed RIVM layer; nearest facilities are external straight-line references, not accessible capacity.

causalTrace.summary: Numerical ledgers reconcile, but synthetic causal stages omit local mechanisms, accountable authority, source validity and physical dependency provenance.
notes: Scenario contributions are visible and exact, but they are model assumptions rather than measurements or operator assessments.

The evidence set includes static registers, adopted plans, future projects, an official risk profile, dated observations, a short forecast and ended historical events; these classes must not be collapsed into one current-state layer.

T+48/T+72 Waterinfo, live asset positions, operator topology, visitors, hospital acceptance and route state are Unknown/NoData. Numerically neutral missingness must not be presented as zero hazard or restored service.

recovery72h.summary: First-72-hour degradation and recovery lack incident-specific actions, owners, prerequisites, resources and completion evidence.
notes: River has seven exactly unchanged service values from T+24 through T+72 while Facilities declines further; compound remains broadly degraded through T+72. Other presets return affected population to zero through generic curves without operator milestones.

At T+0-6 select event, authority, valid window, dike/stream/control state, ignition/target, warning, visitor/institution exposure and cross-region lead. At T+6-24 track roads/rail/ferries, water assets, hospitals, vulnerable-person contact and operator assessments.

At T+24-72 track shelter/support-point staffing and stock, resupply, water quality/pressure, sewer/RWZI state, hospital acceptance, access restoration, containment, welfare, controlled return and evidence-backed completion.
Every transition needs owner, action, prerequisite, resource, issued/valid time, evidence class, progress and completion; absence or expiry remains Unknown.

findings.summary: Official 2025 identity, boundary, places and population reconcile.
findings.evidence: E01 verifies GM1734, its contained centre, 48,945 residents, ninety neighbourhoods, twelve BAG places, 25 BRT settlement labels and unique safety-region assignment. Neighbourhood population differs by only fifteen residents (-0.031%).
findings.action: Retain official identity/boundary, independent BAG/BRT roles, transparent fifteen-person reconciliation and field-level null semantics; do not alter rounded source observations.

findings.summary: The river preset publishes unsupported local inundation precision without a selected dike-ring-43 scenario.
findings.evidence: The model gives a 2.391544 legacy depth-like amplitude, 20,199 affected at T+24 and 21,567 at T+72. E02-E04 establish Rhine/Waal/Linge water management, dike reinforcement context and interregional ring-43 planning, but no breach/reach, boundary conditions, defence state, arrival time or licensed footprint drives the result. The model type explicitly says the amplitude is not hydraulic-model water depth.
findings.action: Retain river plausibility and normalized stress as an internal diagnostic, but suppress metre/depth, affected and hotspot claims until a governed LIWO/WSRL/RWS scenario supplies issue/validity, breach/reach, boundaries, defence/control state, arrival and licensed extent/depth. Suppression must not imply safety.

findings.summary: Unrelated active hazards reuse one nearly identical neighbourhood hotspot order.
findings.evidence: At T+24, severe storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber, wildfire and compound are led by the same small set—Lingebuurt, Kern Herveld/Kern Oosterhout, Groenoord and de Wuurde—despite distinct mechanisms documented by E02-E04 and E10.
findings.action: Replace the common hash with hazard-specific, versioned spatial evidence. Unsupported maps must render Unknown without numeric hotspot labels; a supported hazard field should remain consistent across service views but not across unrelated hazards.

findings.summary: Pluvial, groundwater and drought outputs omit the controlled Over-Betuwe water system.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 reports amplitude 0.366688, 3,831 affected and Drainage 0.573926, then zero affected at T+72. E02 establishes Linge, soil/height, GGOR, best-effort target levels and dry-period shortfall; E07 has 206 partial assets; E08 has only Driel point forecasts through T+24. No rainfall field, antecedent groundwater, sewer/ditch catchment, asset state, receiving level or drainage milestone drives the curve.
findings.action: Ingest versioned pluvial/AHN and groundwater evidence with rainfall/duration, Linge/ditch receiving levels, target/control state, sewer/pump/RWZI topology and road thresholds. Keep T+48/T+72 and null capacities Unknown; suppress exact local depth/rank/recovery until evidenced.

findings.summary: Logical road links omit ferry, rail, internal crossing and external-care operational dependencies.
findings.evidence: E05-E06 identify A15/A50/A325/N837, two stations, scheduled stops and four ferries, while E09 shows all nearest acute care outside GM1734. The graph lacks internal roads/crossings, ferry state, train/freight operation, Betuweroute separation, vehicles, water-level constraints, closures and hospital acceptance. Same-corridor links are series, not independent capacity.
findings.action: Build a typed multimodal graph with internal routes, bridges/tunnels, ferry modes, passenger/freight rail, valid NDW/ProRail/authority state, vehicle/crew availability and destination-specific hospital acceptance. Never infer passability or capacity from static geometry, schedule presence or nearest straight-line distance.

findings.summary: Betuweroute hazardous-goods and historic closure context are not represented with valid lifecycle semantics.
findings.evidence: E04 identifies road/rail/water toxic-substance transport and Betuweroute preparative arrangements. E05 records a Valburg freight stoppage that explicitly ended on 2026-04-10. The simulator has neither a hazardous-goods release/plume/cordon pathway nor a current operational rail feed.
findings.action: Add a separately selectable, source-contained hazardous-material scenario with substance, release point/time, weather, plume/cordon, responder access and validity. Expired disruptions must close; absence of a live feed remains Unknown rather than normal operation.

findings.summary: Exact utility, wastewater, telecom and facility trajectories exceed the public evidence.
findings.evidence: E07 supplies 206 water points, one grid-planning sample, 110 antenna sites and 35 education records, but lacks dependable topology, live state, capacity units, power/backhaul dependencies, occupancy and repair resources. E09 provides only external care roles/distances. Cyber T+24 still reports 12,165 affected and Telecom 0.459092 without a target.
findings.action: Keep public assets as provenance-rich non-causal context and label service values synthetic indices. Permit physical propagation only from operator-approved topology/state and a named cyber/physical target; sensitive or absent pipe, feeder, backhaul, care and backup data remains Unknown.

findings.summary: Wildfire and affected-population outputs omit ignition, fuels and dynamic recreation/event exposure.
findings.evidence: Canonical wildfire at T+24 reports zero flame, smoke 0.472002, 1,825 affected and exact service losses without ignition or plume. E10 establishes nature/recreation and accessible visitors; E05 demonstrates dated Vierdaagse and ferry transients. Resident allocation does not capture event-time visitors, commuters, rail/ferry users or support needs.
findings.action: Add official combustible-area eligibility, ignition/perimeter, fuel/moisture, valid wind, barriers, roads, water points and suppression resources. Model privacy-preserving, timestamped transient/institution exposure separately from CBS residents; missing occupancy remains Unknown.

findings.summary: First-72-hour service status lacks accountable action, resources and completion evidence.
findings.evidence: River service values mostly plateau from T+24 to T+72 while Facilities worsens; compound retains 23,442 affected at T+72. Other hazards generically return affected population to zero. E02-E10 require water-board, safety-region, municipal, transport, land-manager, utility and care decisions that are absent from the causal ledger.
findings.action: For each T+0/6/12/24/48/72 transition record authority, action, target, prerequisite, resource, issued/valid time, evidence class, progress, blocker and completion. Track warnings, evacuation/shelter, vulnerable-person contact, ferry/road/rail access, hospitals, water quality/assets, utility inspection, resupply, containment and controlled return.

findings.summary: Missing or expired forecasts, asset state, routes and capacity can be misread as zero or safe.
findings.evidence: E01 has 0/90 coverage for two fields; E07 contains null/ambiguous asset records and one grid sample; E08 ends at T+24; E09 has no local acute-care point; E05 includes expired event/disruption evidence. None supports zero infrastructure, safe water, open route, available care or restored service.
findings.action: Expose publisher, edition, observed/issued/valid/retrieved time, coverage, licence and evidence class per field. Render Unknown/NoData explicitly and numerically neutral; never convert it to zero, safe, empty, closed, available, unavailable or restored.

corrections.summary: Gate GM1734 river output behind a governed dike-ring-43/Rhine-Waal-Linge scenario and correct legacy amplitude presentation.
corrections.validation: Without selected reach/breach, boundaries, defence/control state, issue/validity, arrival and licensed extent/depth, keep amplitude diagnostic only, never append metres, mark spatial evidence unsupported and render affected/hotspots Unknown; verify unresolved river risk is not presented as safe.

corrections.summary: Integrate versioned Over-Betuwe pluvial, groundwater, Linge, drainage and water-control evidence.
corrections.validation: Verify publisher, edition, rainfall duration, units, licence, target/control validity and NoData; require antecedent groundwater, receiving levels, catchments, pump/RWZI state and road thresholds before calculating Drainage or recovery.

corrections.summary: Replace the shared neighbourhood seed with hazard-specific local evidence and source-contained fire/cyber adapters.
corrections.validation: Unrelated hazards must not share one neighbourhood order; fire requires eligible fuel plus ignition/perimeter/wind, cyber requires a named target/topology, and unsupported maps render Unknown without precision labels.

corrections.summary: Build typed road, ferry, rail, hazardous-goods and external-care dependency context.
corrections.validation: Verify series corridor identity, internal crossings, ferry mode/state, passenger/freight separation and hospital destinations; require valid closure/passability, vehicle/crew, rail/ferry operation and hospital acceptance before asserting reachability.

corrections.summary: Keep public water, grid, telecom, education and care records provenance-rich and non-causal until approved topology/state exists.
corrections.validation: Registers expose publisher, edition, retrieval/validity, coverage, licence and evidence class; null/ambiguous lifecycle, one-sample coverage and missing topology remain Unknown and cannot drive exact service percentages or restoration.

corrections.summary: Add separate dynamic exposure and an accountable GM1734 first-72-hour action/resource ledger.
corrections.validation: Keep residents, timestamped visitors/commuters and institutional occupancy distinct; snapshot T+0/6/12/24/48/72 authority, action, prerequisites, resources, issued/valid time, progress, blocker and completion; reject operational/restored claims without evidence.

residualLimitations: No selected dike-ring-43 breach/reach, Rhine/Waal/Linge boundary conditions, defence/control state, arrival time or licensed inundation footprint is causally consumed.
The reported 2.391544 field is a legacy normalized depth-like amplitude, explicitly not surveyed or hydraulic-model metres.
No versioned municipal pluvial raster, AHN flow path, antecedent groundwater, sewer/ditch topology, road threshold or dewatering state is connected to the exercise clock.
Streefpeil/GGOR and future dike reinforcement are governance/design evidence, not live level, current capacity, failure probability or restoration.
Waterinfo observations are point/time specific and the forecast ends at T+24; T+48/T+72 remain NoData.
The HWH snapshot is partial; duplicate/lifecycle semantics, reported capacity units, catchments, control positions, power dependencies and repair state are unavailable.
One Liander capacity-planning sample does not establish GM1734 feeder coverage, live load, switching, damage, reserve or repair.
RDI antenna installations do not establish coverage, traffic, backhaul, battery endurance, availability or restoration.
Education registrations do not prove occupancy, shelter designation, stock, accessibility, backup power or activation.
No live ignition, perimeter, fuel/moisture, valid wind, visitor count, access, extinguishing water or suppression dataset is causally consumed.
Resident totals omit event-time visitors, commuters, rail/ferry users and institutional populations; dated annual events cannot be carried into the present.
Eight NWB links are logical Mobility/Supply proxies; serial A15/A50/A325 segments and nominal capacities are not independent corridors or measured throughput.
Static stations and scheduled stops do not prove incident-time passenger or freight rail, buses, rolling stock or evacuation capacity.
Municipal ferry links do not expose water-level restrictions, schedule validity, vessel/crew state, accessible capacity or emergency priority.
The ended April 2026 Betuweroute disruption is historical and cannot persist; absence of a live rail feed does not prove normal operation.
RIVM roles and straight-line distances do not prove ambulance time, route state, acceptance, staffing, beds, generator endurance or diversion.
No operator-approved drinking-water, electricity, gas, wastewater or telecom network topology/live state is consumed.
